annotations.annotation_text: Page 75 opens Book 1, Chapter 4 ("The Burial of HCE") during the Age of Gods (transition) phase. This passage continues the burial of the giant in the landscape, the archaeological mound, the Four Annalists surveying history, featuring HCE, Mamalujo, Kate the Slop. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: HCE is buried in the landscape, his sleeping body echoing the myth of the giant Finn MacCool, whose body supposedly forms the geography of Dublin.
sources: Mink, Louis O. A Finnegans Wake Gazetteer. https://archive.org/details/finneganswakegaz0000mink

annotations.annotation_text: The Four Old Men (Mamalujo) survey HCE's grave, functioning as historians or annalists examining the past.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas

annotations.annotation_text: The burial mound links Irish prehistoric cairns with Egyptian pyramids, transforming the Dublin landscape into a site of universal mythic resonance.
sources: Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 75 ("The Burial of HCE"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods (transition) dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Kate the Slop: the female domestic figure who tends the house and by extension, the grave/mound, embodying the cyclical continuity of life.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp

annotations.annotation_text: The archaeological mound is also the midden-heap where the mysterious letter from Boston is found, equating the buried giant with the buried text.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind

annotations.annotation_text: The act of surveying the grave by Mamalujo parodies antiquarian scholarship and the attempt to impose order on the chaotic past.
sources: McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
